Implementation Plan

Implementation plan: ship the default-off `.github/ai/chatgpt_pool.json` (Refs #8969, fixup `fixup-chatgpt-pool-config-file`)

Planning ref: `orchestrator/project-8969` @ `7511e1f7ed272c545c129b3362438cf003dc4cce` (Integration branch mismatch: false).

## Files likely to change
- `.github/ai/chatgpt_pool.json` (new)
- `tests/test_review_chatgpt_reviewer_slot.py`
- `changelog.d/chatgpt-pool-config-file.md` (new)

## Acceptance
ACCEPTANCE: test tests/test_review_chatgpt_reviewer_slot.py::test_shipped_pool_config_file_exists_and_keeps_the_slot_off red-on-base
ACCEPTANCE: test tests/test_review_chatgpt_reviewer_slot.py
ACCEPTANCE: post-merge none: this only adds a data file with the switch off, so no post-merge workflow behaves differently (the slot stays off, and `switch_off` is not logged)

## Automation / scheduler surface (§20.E)
- No new script, supervisor or scheduler wiring. The change adds a data file, one contract test and a changelog fragment.
- Entry point that reads the file, unchanged: the `codex-agent` job of `.github/workflows/review_autofix.yml`, "Resolve AI engine" step. It runs `claude_engine.py chatgpt-slot --config ${GITHUB_WORKSPACE}/.codex-workflow-src/.github/ai/chatgpt_pool.json`. I checked that the job's `.codex-workflow-src` checkout is a full (non-sparse) checkout at `SCRIPT_REF` with `fetch-depth: 1`, so it will contain the new file.
- No database work. No entry is needed in `docs/scripts-pending-removal.md` (its existing preflight check at line 402 already names this file).

## Functions or modules to implement
1. `.github/ai/chatgpt_pool.json` (new). JSON, 2-space indentation, keys in the plan's order, trailing newline:
   ```
   {
     "reviewer_slot_enabled": false,
     "model": "gpt-6-sol",
     "replaces": "openai/gpt-6-luna",
     "reasoning": "xhigh"
   }
   ```
   `reviewer_slot_enabled` stays `false`. Turning it on is the separate go-live PR.
2. `tests/test_review_chatgpt_reviewer_slot.py`: add one test, `test_shipped_pool_config_file_exists_and_keeps_the_slot_off`. Put it right after `test_shipped_config_keeps_the_slot_off` (line 113) in the "chatgpt-slot / chatgpt-classify" block. It asserts:
   - `POOL_CONFIG.is_file()`, with a message that names the missing file. It reads `POOL_CONFIG` directly, not through `_shipped_config_text()`, so a missing file fails the test instead of falling back.
   - `json.loads(POOL_CONFIG.read_text(encoding="utf-8"))` is a `dict` equal to `json.loads(SHIPPED_CONFIG)`, and its `reviewer_slot_enabled` is `False`.
   - Running `subprocess.run([sys.executable, str(ENGINE), "chatgpt-slot", "--config", str(POOL_CONFIG)], env=_env(), capture_output=True, text=True, check=True)` prints exactly one stdout line. Parsed the same way `_slot()` parses (split on spaces, then on the first `=`), the line has `enabled == "false"` and `reason == "switch_off"`. It also asserts `source == "file"`, which proves the real file was read rather than defaults.
   - The existing `_slot()` helper is not used, because it copies content into `tmp_path` and the issue wants the shipped path passed straight to `--config`.
   - `_shipped_config_text`, `SHIPPED_CONFIG` and every other test stay untouched.
3. `changelog.d/chatgpt-pool-config-file.md` (new). The first line is `<!-- changelog: fixed -->`, followed by one bullet in the style of `changelog.d/wfopt-2026-10-07-3-idle-test-quoting.md`. The bullet says:
   - `.github/ai/chatgpt_pool.json` now ships with `reviewer_slot_enabled: false` and the plan's `model` / `replaces` / `reasoning` values.
   - Before this, the file was missing and the slot resolved to `config_missing`. It was still off, but the go-live switch had no file to edit.
   - A new test locks the shipped file.
   - The review panel's behaviour is unchanged.
   - Ends with `Refs #8969.` and no closing keyword.

## Data structures affected
- New committed config object with four keys: `reviewer_slot_enabled` (bool), `model` (str), `replaces` (str), `reasoning` (str). These are the keys `resolve_chatgpt_slot` already validates (planning-ref `scripts/claude_engine.py` lines 225-285: `CHATGPT_MODEL_RE`, `CHATGPT_REPLACES_RE`, `CHATGPT_REASONING`). Nothing else changes.

## API or interface changes
- None. The `chatgpt-slot` CLI, the step outputs (`chatgpt_slot`, `chatgpt_model`, `chatgpt_replaces`, `chatgpt_reasoning`), the env vars and the log keys are unchanged. With the file present, the resolver's reason for the off state goes from `config_missing` to `switch_off`, and `source` goes from `default` to `file`. `enabled` stays `false`.

## Decisions
### D1 — Call the CLI on the shipped path in a new test instead of changing the fallback test
- Chosen: add a separate test that asserts the file exists and runs `chatgpt-slot --config POOL_CONFIG` directly.
- Alternatives considered: remove the `_shipped_config_text` fallback so the existing test fails when the file is missing; or have the new test reuse `_slot()` with the file's text.
- Why: the issue forbids changing `_shipped_config_text` or any other test. `_slot()` writes a temporary copy, so it would not prove the shipped path is the one being read.

### D2 — Multi-line, 2-space formatted JSON
- Chosen: one key per line, 2-space indentation, trailing newline, keys in the plan's order.
- Alternatives considered: the single-line literal exactly as `SHIPPED_CONFIG` writes it.
- Why: the issue asks for 2-space indentation. The test compares parsed objects, so formatting cannot break it, and the go-live PR stays a one-line diff on `reviewer_slot_enabled`.

### D3 — Changelog kind `fixed`
- Chosen: `<!-- changelog: fixed -->`.
- Alternatives considered: `added`.
- Why: the issue requires the `fixed` marker. The file was documented as shipped (in `changelog.d/chatgpt-reviewer-slot.md` and `agents.d/chatgpt-reviewer-slot.md`) but was missing, so this corrects a defect.

## Security considerations
- Trust boundary: the workflow reads only the trusted support checkout's copy (`.codex-workflow-src`), never the PR head. That is unchanged.
- The new file holds no secrets, credentials or account data, only a model slug, the slug it replaces, a reasoning level and a boolean.
- Shipping `false` keeps the credential path off: the ChatGPT pool token step and the relay are not used.
- Abuse case: a PR that sets the switch to `true` changes nothing for that PR's own review, because the workflow reads the support copy at `SCRIPT_REF`. It only takes effect after merge into the support ref, which is the intended go-live path.
- No new endpoint, worker or authorization surface. No money handling.

## Potential risks or edge cases
- Workspace artefact (not a planning-ref conflict): in this read-only sandbox, the working-tree copy of `scripts/claude_engine.py` has local modifications and lacks `chatgpt-slot`. The committed planning ref has it (`resolve_chatgpt_slot` at line 225, `config_missing` at line 243, `switch_off` at line 284, CLI parser at line 1693). The issue cites lines 240-243, which is a small line drift with the same logic. The implementer works against the planning-ref content.
- Minor citation drift only. `scripts/claude_engine.py`, `scripts/review_run_reviewers.sh` and the workflow YAML must not change, as the issue requires.
- Off-path logs: `switch_off` produces `AI_ENGINE_FALLBACK ... reason=switch_off action=skip` only on the reviewer-dispatch path when a chatgpt slug is in the panel. With the slot off, no slug is swapped in, so the panel and logs stay as they are. The existing tests `test_off_path_tiers_are_unchanged` and `test_resolve_step_writes_the_slot_outputs` cover this.
- `scripts/review_untrusted_workspace.py` line 145 protects `.github/ai/claude_engine.json` but not the new file. That is acceptable, because the PR-head copy is never read. Adding protection would also be outside the issue's `files_touched`.

## Testing considerations
- `PYTHONDONTWRITEBYTECODE=1 python3 -m pytest -q -p no:cacheprovider tests/test_review_chatgpt_reviewer_slot.py` must pass.
- The new test fails on the base ref (file missing), so it is red-on-base. It passes once the file exists.
- The existing `test_shipped_config_keeps_the_slot_off` now reads the real file through `_shipped_config_text` and must still pass, which also checks the file against the literal.
- Run the changelog fragment validator if CI has one (for example a `changelog.d` lint), and confirm the marker is the first line.

Scope-mode: Hold Scope
Reuse-audit: extends tests/test_review_chatgpt_reviewer_slot.py (POOL_CONFIG, SHIPPED_CONFIG, ENGINE, _env) and claude_engine.py chatgpt-slot
Scope-mode justification: The issue lists three exact files and forbids changes to the resolver, the reviewer script and the workflow YAML. The plan adds the missing data file, one test that reuses the existing module constants and `_env()` helper, and a changelog fragment, with no new helpers. The complete option (asserting the file exists, the parsed values and the CLI's `enabled=false reason=switch_off source=file`) costs only a few lines more than a bare existence check. Under §6 (Security > Correctness & safety > Backward compatibility > Operational clarity > Performance > Speed), completeness supports correctness at no extra risk, so it is chosen.
